courses.title: Junior Salesforce Developer
courses.entry: No previous CRM or Salesforce experience is required. Begin with people, business information, and a personal learning org. Apex syntax and browser-language basics are taught before their application code. Complete the separate workspace guide before code deployment.
courses.exit: Deliver and explain a small Salesforce feature with a deliberate data model, restricted-user access evidence, automation, bulk-aware Apex, a usable interface, tests, and a reproducible handover.
courses.project: Northstar Motors is a fictional dealership. Anna and Max are salespeople, Oleg manages the team, and Irina is a customer requesting a test drive. The project records an appointment and supports a controlled handover.

lessons.title: What a CRM Does for a Business
lessons.outcome: Follow one customer request and discover why a team needs shared information, clear responsibility, and a next action.
lessons.task: Anna will be absent tomorrow. Prepare a short note that lets Max continue helping Irina.
lessons.acceptance: The note distinguishes a request from a confirmed test drive. Another person can state what happens next without guessing.
lessons.interview: Why is a telephone number insufficient?
lessons.visual: two drawn colleagues sharing a customer record, conversation and calendar

lessons.title: Salesforce Products, the Platform, and Your Org
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a product, an application, and an org while learning who uses and changes Salesforce.
lessons.task: Northstar needs a new field, a customer note, an access change, a useful management report, and a stock-system connection.
lessons.acceptance: An application is not confused with an org. The proposed developer work includes understanding requirements and testing, not just writing code.
lessons.interview: What is an org?
lessons.visual: a drawn salesperson, administrator and developer around a single application workspace

lessons.title: Create and Reopen a Learning Org
lessons.outcome: Use a browser to create a personal Salesforce learning environment and verify that you can return to the same one.
lessons.task: Prepare a short environment note that helps you resume learning tomorrow.
lessons.acceptance: The note identifies one learning environment consistently. No passwords, authentication files, or real customer details appear in the evidence.
lessons.interview: Is VS Code required for this lesson?
lessons.visual: a small separate training workspace in a protective outline beside a larger company workspace

lessons.title: Finding Your Way Around Salesforce
lessons.outcome: Recognize an application, navigation item, list, record page, and Setup without assuming previous Salesforce use.
lessons.task: Create a simple map showing how Anna finds a customer and where an administrator changes configuration.
lessons.acceptance: Each interface area has a plain-language purpose. The map distinguishes navigation, stored data, and configuration.
lessons.interview: Does Recently Viewed contain every record?
lessons.visual: one clean application window opening into a list and a single record card

lessons.title: Objects, Fields, and Records
lessons.outcome: Use a small vehicle catalogue to distinguish the shape of information from individual stored items.
lessons.task: Create a diagram containing two vehicles and three test-drive events.
lessons.acceptance: Objects, fields, values, and records are labelled correctly. Vehicle status is distinct from test-drive status.
lessons.interview: Is City EV a field?
lessons.visual: three neatly stacked record cards with aligned property rows and one highlighted field

lessons.title: Turn a Request into a Testable Task
lessons.outcome: Clarify who needs a feature, what information it uses, and how you will know it works before choosing a tool.
lessons.task: Write a one-page brief for Oleg before creating fields or automation.
lessons.acceptance: Assumptions are visibly different from confirmed requirements. Acceptance criteria describe behaviour rather than an unexamined technical solution.
lessons.interview: Can an invented restriction be treated as a requirement?
lessons.visual: a simple request card becoming three concrete checklist steps beside a drawn learner

lessons.title: Choose Standard Objects Before Creating New Ones
lessons.outcome: Classify customer information using Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity, and Case, then explain why the course adds two custom objects.
lessons.task: Explain how Northstar should store five different pieces of customer work.
lessons.acceptance: An Opportunity is not described as requiring a Lead in every process. The course Contact lookup and its limits are stated explicitly. The learning org contains the core Vehicle and Test Drive schema needed by J08, without duplicate objects.
lessons.interview: Is a customer complaint a new sale?
lessons.visual: a restrained row of customer, company, opportunity and support record symbols connected by one path

lessons.title: Field Types, Formulas, and Validation Rules
lessons.outcome: Separate entered values, calculated values, and rejected input using concrete appointment examples.
lessons.task: Give Oleg evidence that the fields accept valid data and explain invalid input.
lessons.acceptance: A historical appointment can receive an unrelated edit without this time rule blocking it. Blank handling and time-zone assumptions are documented.
lessons.interview: When does a validation rule reject a save?
lessons.visual: a record form with a calendar field, a number field and a clear validation check

lessons.title: Choose Lookup or Master-Detail Deliberately
lessons.outcome: Compare relationship behaviour while preserving independent ownership of the course Test Drive records.
lessons.task: Explain why the course keeps Test Drive independently owned.
lessons.acceptance: The experiment does not replace the core relationship. The explanation includes ownership and access, not only deletion.
lessons.interview: Where is a Master-Detail field created?
lessons.visual: two record cards connected by a clean relationship line with a small linked record underneath

lessons.title: Build a Usable Sales Application
lessons.outcome: Assemble tabs, a record page, a useful list, and a small management report around one clear salesperson journey.
lessons.task: Create a short demonstration from application navigation to an appointment and a management count.
lessons.acceptance: The report matches the known sample records. The explanation does not claim that a page layout enforces field-level security.
lessons.interview: Why can a report and a list show different counts?
lessons.visual: a compact car-dealership application window with a car, appointment card and small bar chart

lessons.title: Understand the Layers of Data Access
lessons.outcome: Separate sign-in, object operations, field permissions, and access to an individual record.
lessons.task: Explain why similar symptoms require different investigation paths.
lessons.acceptance: Object, field, and record access are distinguished. Administrator results are not represented as salesperson tests.
lessons.interview: Will record sharing grant object Read?
lessons.visual: four translucent geometric access layers protecting one customer record

lessons.title: Grant a Small Set of Working Permissions
lessons.outcome: Create an additive permission set that enables appointment work without broad administration.
lessons.task: Submit a small table connecting Anna to the operations and fields she needs.
lessons.acceptance: The evidence uses a restricted user. The explanation recognizes additive permissions and independent record sharing.
lessons.interview: Does an unchecked Delete box remove another Delete grant?
lessons.visual: two small permission cards combining to open one lock on a record

lessons.title: Set a Record-Access Baseline and Add Exceptions
lessons.outcome: Use Private defaults, roles, and a focused sharing rule to explain appointment visibility.
lessons.task: Explain the intended owner, peer, manager, and service-reviewer access.
lessons.acceptance: A role is not confused with a profile. No unsupported branch isolation is claimed. Other granting sources are investigated when results differ.
lessons.interview: Does Private prevent all non-owner access?
lessons.visual: a simple team hierarchy above three record cards with carefully drawn access paths

lessons.title: Share One Record and Test an Ownership Change
lessons.outcome: Use manual sharing for a specific handover and verify transfer behaviour in the actual org configuration.
lessons.task: Explain the behaviour of one manual share before and after ownership changes.
lessons.acceptance: The explanation does not say manual shares always disappear. New ownership is not mistaken for retained manual sharing.
lessons.interview: Does sharing transfer ownership?
lessons.visual: one drawn colleague handing a single record card to another through a permission key

lessons.title: Trace the Source of an Access Problem
lessons.outcome: Investigate missing or excessive access with evidence, one hypothesis, and a minimal correction.
lessons.task: Diagnose one object, one field, and one record access case.
lessons.acceptance: A layout issue is not mislabeled as FLS. A filter issue is not mislabeled as sharing. Any unavailable execution check is stated honestly.
lessons.interview: Why inspect Access Granted By?
lessons.visual: a magnifying glass tracing two different paths toward the same accessible record

lessons.title: Verify Access for Sales, Service, and Management
lessons.outcome: Turn a written access matrix into repeatable positive and negative checks for three working personas.
lessons.task: Deliver a short access demonstration and an evidence matrix for Oleg.
lessons.acceptance: No broad grant was added solely to make a test pass. Every executed result names the tested persona. Untested cells remain distinguishable from successful ones.
lessons.interview: Is a persona the same as a role?
lessons.visual: two drawn workplace roles facing the same records with different visible subsets

lessons.title: Create a Record-Triggered Flow with a Clear Failure Path
lessons.outcome: Create one follow-up Task for a new appointment request, avoid update duplicates, and make a failed reminder visible.
lessons.task: Deliver the Flow, activity-setting change, and a three-case result table.
lessons.acceptance: The activity prerequisite is included. The submission distinguishes a Task from an email notification. The active version and observed transaction outcome are stated.
lessons.interview: Why choose after-save here?
lessons.visual: three simple flow nodes transforming a saved appointment into a reminder card

lessons.title: Apex Syntax, Variables, Collections, and Methods
lessons.outcome: Read and write a small pure Apex function before introducing database operations.
lessons.task: Add a method that returns labels for available minutes using a Map.
lessons.acceptance: The code performs no database operation. Returned ordering and null behaviour are explicit. The explanation distinguishes List, Set, and Map.
lessons.interview: How does assignment differ from comparison?
lessons.visual: a calm developer workspace with a small code card, a collection of blocks and a method-shaped container

lessons.title: Read and Change Records with SOQL and DML
lessons.outcome: Write a bounded bulk operation with explicit user-mode access and separate reads from writes.
lessons.task: Provide evidence for empty, single-record, and 200-record scenarios.
lessons.acceptance: No query or DML is executed once per appointment. Only Requested appointments for supplied vehicles change. The stated dataset boundary is honest.
lessons.interview: Does assigning a field in memory save it?
lessons.visual: one data shelf with a clean read arrow and a separate update arrow returning one record

lessons.title: Use a Thin Trigger and a Focused Handler
lessons.outcome: Validate the whole incoming collection while keeping business rules outside the trigger entry point.
lessons.task: Implement and explain the two agreed validation rules.
lessons.acceptance: All pending records are checked. The handler contains no unnecessary self-update. The submission states what the rules do not guarantee.
lessons.interview: Why use old values?
lessons.visual: an incoming group of record cards activating one event-driven processing node

lessons.title: Trace Automation Through a Transaction
lessons.outcome: Explain how several automations participate in one save and verify what a rollback actually removes.
lessons.task: Produce a small timeline and before-and-after record evidence.
lessons.acceptance: The timeline is labelled as a relevant subset of the official order. A retained variable ID is not mistaken for a committed record. Separate asynchronous work is not described as the same transaction.
lessons.interview: Does a generated ID prove commit?
lessons.visual: an orderly sequence of four process tiles inside one transaction boundary

lessons.title: Write Apex Tests That Prove Behaviour
lessons.outcome: Create independent test data and assert valid, invalid, and bulk outcomes rather than aiming only for executed lines.
lessons.task: Test the pure function and appointment validation with independent data.
lessons.acceptance: Assertions check the intended business outcome. Tests do not depend on ordinary org data. The submitted results come from an actual run or are clearly marked unperformed.
lessons.interview: Can 100% coverage accompany incorrect behaviour?
lessons.visual: a small test bench comparing an expected result card with an actual result card and one check

lessons.title: HTML, JavaScript, and Your First Lightning Web Component
lessons.outcome: Learn the browser-language basics and build an explicitly simulated appointment preview with four visible states.
lessons.task: Extend the simulated preview with a second sample appointment while preserving honest labels.
lessons.acceptance: The interface is explicitly labelled as a demonstration. Sample rows are not claimed to be persisted. Every rendered row has a stable key.
lessons.interview: Does assigning rows create Salesforce records?
lessons.visual: three clean interface building blocks assembling into one component card

lessons.title: Read and Edit a Record with Lightning Data Service
lessons.outcome: Use a standard record form for an ordinary edit and verify the result under a restricted user.
lessons.task: Deliver the working editor and a short comparison with a custom Apex alternative.
lessons.acceptance: No synthetic preview ID is used as a Salesforce record ID. The outcome is verified after save. The choice of standard components is justified.
lessons.interview: Does @api recordId always populate in every container?
lessons.visual: a small component window connected to a shared data cache and a record card

lessons.title: Pass Data Down and Send Events Up
lessons.outcome: Split a small interface into a parent and child with clear ownership of state.
lessons.task: Extend the example with a third simulated item and document the public contract.
lessons.acceptance: The child does not mutate the supplied object. Events use a clear matching name and minimal detail. The simulation is not described as a database operation.
lessons.interview: Who owns selectedId?
lessons.visual: a parent component container and two child cards communicating with one upward event arrow

lessons.title: Investigate a Failure from Symptom to Cause
lessons.outcome: Use a reproducible case, a focused hypothesis, and the right evidence from the browser or Salesforce.
lessons.task: Choose the event mismatch or another controlled learning failure and explain it from symptom to proof.
lessons.acceptance: The note separates observed facts from hypotheses. The correction addresses the demonstrated cause. Private data and credentials are excluded.
lessons.interview: Why is a hypothesis different from an observation?
lessons.visual: a magnifying glass isolating one highlighted break in an otherwise clean code path

lessons.title: Use Git to Hand Over a Reproducible Change
lessons.outcome: Capture the relevant metadata, review a small diff, and submit a version another person can inspect.
lessons.task: Hand over the appointment feature as a versioned, explainable change.
lessons.acceptance: The package excludes credentials and real customer data. Setup-only changes required by the feature are captured or explicitly documented. The review target is an identifiable version in the learner repository.
lessons.interview: Does changing a local file change the org immediately?
lessons.visual: a tidy branching path of commits joining a reviewed change card

lessons.title: Deliver the Northstar Test-Drive Application
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate a complete small feature, explain its boundaries, and respond to a modest requirement change.
lessons.task: Deliver a short demonstration, source package, and review note for the Northstar appointment feature.
lessons.acceptance: The feature works within its stated educational scope. Critical correctness or access defects are corrected before requesting acceptance. The author can explain data, permissions, automation, code, and interface choices. No simulation or unexecuted test is misrepresented as a live result.
lessons.interview: What makes this more than a collection of exercises?
lessons.visual: a finished car test-drive application with a calendar and a small review check

courses.title: Middle Salesforce Developer
courses.entry: Complete the Junior foundations or demonstrate a small feature with a sound data model, least-privilege access, bulk-safe Apex, meaningful tests, and a basic LWC. CRM and the Northstar actors are restated where needed; unfamiliar product licenses are not assumed.
courses.exit: Build and explain an integrated feature with explicit security, durable operation identity, controlled asynchronous work, failure recovery, usable UI states, and reproducible release evidence.
courses.project: Northstar Motors: Anna and Max manage customer test drives and warranty requests; Oleg supervises work; Irina is a fictional customer. The core project uses custom Vehicle and Test Drive records, then explicitly declared request and diagnostic metadata.

lessons.title: Designing and verifying an access model
lessons.outcome: Turn a business request into separate object, field, record, and operation decisions. Build an access matrix for two sales branches before changing permissions.
lessons.task: Prepare and verify a minimum-permission model for Anna, Max, and Oleg.
lessons.acceptance: Every allowed row identifies its grant. At least three denied operations are tested. No administrator-only evidence is presented as salesperson verification.
lessons.interview: Does object Read grant every record?
lessons.visual: Four nested access gates surrounding one appointment card

lessons.title: Permission Set Groups and muting
lessons.outcome: Predict effective permissions when a permission set group mutes a grant that is also supplied elsewhere.
lessons.task: Submit the four-path experiment with a small diagram and observed results.
lessons.acceptance: The explanation distinguishes group-local muting from effective user permissions. All four assignment combinations are considered. Group recalculation and unchanged record access are recorded.
lessons.interview: Does muting alter the reused permission set?
lessons.visual: Several permission paths converging on one field with a single path blocked

lessons.title: Manual and implicit sharing
lessons.outcome: Identify why a record is visible and distinguish an explicit manual grant from access arising from supported standard relationships.
lessons.task: Produce a short before-and-after report for manual sharing and one supported implicit-sharing relationship.
lessons.acceptance: Each visibility result names an access mechanism. Remaining access after removal is investigated. No claim says all lookups automatically share records.
lessons.interview: Does a manual Read share grant field Read?
lessons.visual: One appointment reached by a manual bridge and a separate relationship bridge

lessons.title: Apex managed sharing across a record lifecycle
lessons.outcome: Maintain a manager's record access while preserving unrelated grants and handling bulk changes.
lessons.task: Implement the transition table on Project__c and submit evidence of safe reconciliation.
lessons.acceptance: No unrelated share is deleted. Cleared and changed managers remove the obsolete owned grant. Bulk and undelete behavior are explicitly tested.
lessons.interview: Why use a custom reason?
lessons.visual: A project card transfers one access key while an unrelated key remains untouched

lessons.title: Restriction rules and supported access paths
lessons.outcome: Filter an already accessible record set for selected users while recognizing object, edition, and execution-context boundaries.
lessons.task: Create the North/South experiment and explain the result for two users.
lessons.acceptance: No new access is attributed to the restriction. Supported object, edition, and context are recorded. Positive, negative, and unaffected-user cases are included.
lessons.interview: Can the rule open a private appointment?
lessons.visual: An already open collection of appointment cards passing through a regional filter

lessons.title: Apex security and API-version defaults
lessons.outcome: Separate class sharing context from database access mode and verify security when changing an Apex API version.
lessons.task: Explain and verify one read path under explicit modes and API-version defaults.
lessons.acceptance: The report separates sharing from CRUD/FLS. API versions are identified. No broad permission is added solely to make the test green.
lessons.interview: Is omitted sharing always without sharing?
lessons.visual: Two versioned execution lanes with separate record and field access gates

lessons.title: Choosing Flow or Apex for a business operation
lessons.outcome: Choose an implementation from the shape of the work, its transaction boundaries, and the team's ability to maintain it.
lessons.task: Choose and implement the confirmation rule, then explain how two larger variants would change your decision.
lessons.acceptance: The choice mentions maintenance and volume. No duplicate automation performs the same responsibility. The failure policy is demonstrated rather than implied.
lessons.interview: Is Flow always preferable for a simple UI?
lessons.visual: One business operation branching toward three simple implementation tools

lessons.title: Order of execution, recursion, and idempotency
lessons.outcome: Explain repeated automation within a transaction and design a durable business result that is not duplicated by re-entry or retries.
lessons.task: Build the declared receipt behavior and demonstrate repeated execution without duplicate results.
lessons.acceptance: Exactly one receipt exists per defined key. Unrelated failures are not called successful retries. The confirmation-cycle limitation is explicit.
lessons.interview: Why does static state not solve a later retry?
lessons.visual: A circular automation path feeding a single durable receipt slot

lessons.title: Structuring Apex and using Custom Metadata
lessons.outcome: Separate warranty business rules, orchestration, and external access without adding layers that have no clear responsibility.
lessons.task: Separate one policy and one business decision from a mixed orchestration sketch.
lessons.acceptance: Dependencies are visible at the entry point. Local tests require no provider or real credentials. Each introduced layer has a stated responsibility.
lessons.interview: Why is request progress ordinary data?
lessons.visual: One large code block separated into policy orchestration and adapter blocks

lessons.title: Testing a complete local business rule
lessons.outcome: Build independent fixtures and meaningful assertions for normal, boundary, invalid, and bulk inputs before introducing network behavior.
lessons.task: Submit a local test suite with boundaries, negative cases, and mixed bulk input.
lessons.acceptance: No business records are read through SeeAllData. Strict cutoff and protected statuses are checked. The mutation fails a relevant assertion.
lessons.interview: Why pass a cutoff instead of reading now everywhere?
lessons.visual: A boundary marker separating one cancelled appointment from three protected appointments

lessons.title: Selecting an asynchronous processing mechanism
lessons.outcome: Match delayed work to its volume, timing, transaction, and recovery requirements without promising immediate execution.
lessons.task: Choose mechanisms for five operations and state the visible result and recovery behavior of each.
lessons.acceptance: Every delayed operation has a pending state or equivalent acknowledgement. Timing is described as a requirement, not an unsupported guarantee. Retry load is included.
lessons.interview: Does enqueue success prove business success?
lessons.visual: Five business tasks sorted into immediate queue batch schedule and event lanes

lessons.title: Queueable Apex and observable request state
lessons.outcome: Create a local background warranty check with a durable request identity, a job reference, and explicit outcomes before adding HTTP.
lessons.task: Implement the local Queueable lifecycle and a bounded manual retry.
lessons.acceptance: One key creates one business request. Job and request IDs are distinguishable. Failed work is visible and retries are bounded.
lessons.interview: Why pass a request ID?
lessons.visual: One warranty request card linked to two distinct background job attempts

lessons.title: Batch Apex and independent execution scopes
lessons.outcome: Process a larger appointment dataset in bounded transactions and report partial failure without implying whole-job atomicity.
lessons.task: Build the cancellation Batch with visible success, skipped, and failed outcomes.
lessons.acceptance: Protected statuses remain unchanged. An error is visible and tied to its record or scope. A repeat run does not corrupt already processed records.
lessons.interview: What persists with Stateful?
lessons.visual: Three processing trays with independent success and failure markers

lessons.title: Scheduling, workload limits, and monitoring
lessons.outcome: Run periodic work with a deliberate overlap policy, time-zone definition, and observable completion.
lessons.task: Add a schedule and a documented monitoring and recovery procedure to M13.
lessons.acceptance: Time-zone assumptions are explicit. Overlap and abandoned-run behavior are defined. The report distinguishes scheduling, execution, and business completion.
lessons.interview: Why can a nightly job overlap?
lessons.visual: A night schedule with one active processing window and a blocked overlapping run

lessons.title: API contracts and credential boundaries
lessons.outcome: Describe the warranty provider's request, response, errors, and identity before connecting a client.
lessons.task: Create a contract and credential responsibility map that another developer can implement without guessing.
lessons.acceptance: Business negative and transport failures differ. Identity and principal permission mapping are explicit. No secret appears in code or documentation.
lessons.interview: What does the Named Credential contribute?
lessons.visual: A request passing through a separate identity key and endpoint gate

lessons.title: Working with REST and SOAP service contracts
lessons.outcome: Read an existing provider interface, select the appropriate client and mock, and preserve its error and authentication semantics.
lessons.task: Write a contract map and demonstrate the appropriate mock for one concrete client.
lessons.acceptance: The selected mock matches the call mechanism. Example XML is not described as a complete WSDL. Live authentication remains an explicitly separate check.
lessons.interview: Must a modern integration use REST?
lessons.visual: Two request envelopes one structured JSON and one nested XML meeting a common result

lessons.title: HTTP callouts, failures, and bounded retries
lessons.outcome: Implement a small warranty client and test success, invalid responses, business absence, throttling, server failure, and transport errors locally.
lessons.task: Implement the mock and bounded orchestration mapping around the supplied client.
lessons.acceptance: All tests run without a provider. A valid negative answer differs from failure. Retry exhaustion is visible and does not loop indefinitely.
lessons.interview: Is covered=false an error?
lessons.visual: One HTTP response split into distinct success missing throttled and invalid outcomes

lessons.title: Inbound APIs, external IDs, and duplicate protection
lessons.outcome: Accept repeated incoming data without creating duplicate business requests, while distinguishing record identity from operation identity.
lessons.task: Build and verify a stable inbound request contract with conflict handling.
lessons.acceptance: One request exists for three identical deliveries. A successful request is not silently restarted. Conflicting key reuse returns an explicit error.
lessons.interview: What does upsert guarantee conceptually?
lessons.visual: Three repeated request envelopes entering one unique business-record slot

lessons.title: Integration diagnostics and controlled recovery
lessons.outcome: Trace a warranty request across attempts and give an operator enough evidence to retry safely without exposing secrets.
lessons.task: Demonstrate how one request can be found, diagnosed, and safely retried.
lessons.acceptance: History survives later success. One correlation key connects request and attempts. Retry authorization and eligibility are explicit.
lessons.interview: Why retain failed attempts after success?
lessons.visual: One request timeline with preserved failed and successful attempt markers

lessons.title: Choosing SOQL or SOSL for a search requirement
lessons.outcome: Use structured queries for known filters and indexed search for words across object types, while handling delayed search visibility.
lessons.task: Create the appointment list and customer search with distinct contracts.
lessons.acceptance: Date boundaries and null lookups are handled. Multiple object types are distinguishable. The indexing limitation is explained without fabricated timing.
lessons.interview: Why use SOQL for tomorrow's appointments?
lessons.visual: A precise calendar filter beside a magnifying glass spanning three record types

lessons.title: Lightning Web Component lifecycle
lessons.outcome: Observe creation, attachment, rendering, removal, and child-error handling without assuming a component renders only once.
lessons.task: Produce a parent-child trace and correct one deliberately introduced duplicate-resource or render-loop defect.
lessons.acceptance: Hook order is observed rather than invented. Repeated rendering is expected. No duplicated external listener remains after reopening.
lessons.interview: Does renderedCallback run only once?
lessons.visual: A component instance moving through creation attachment repeated rendering and removal

lessons.title: Wire, imperative Apex, and refreshing data
lessons.outcome: Separate reactive reads from explicit writes and refresh the cache that actually supplies the displayed data.
lessons.task: Implement a reactive read and explicit confirmation with separate save and refresh outcomes.
lessons.acceptance: The correct refresh API matches each data source. A successful save is not reported as a failed save. Rapid input changes do not display the wrong record.
lessons.interview: What must be passed to refreshApex?
lessons.visual: A saved appointment beside three distinct cache paths with one selected refresh arrow

lessons.title: DOM events and Lightning Message Service
lessons.outcome: Choose a communication contract for related components and for independent regions of the same Lightning application.
lessons.task: Demonstrate DOM events for one component tree and LMS for a separate panel.
lessons.acceptance: Payloads contain only needed identifiers. DOM and LMS responsibilities are distinct. Scope and cleanup behavior are explained.
lessons.interview: When is a DOM event simpler?
lessons.visual: A small upward component event beside a bridge between two independent page panels

lessons.title: Accessible LWC states and Jest tests
lessons.outcome: Test what a user can understand and operate, including keyboard interaction, empty results, failed loading, and selection events.
lessons.task: Build the four UI states and verify selection and recovery behavior.
lessons.acceptance: Tests pass independently with cleanup. Event payload and error recovery are asserted. Keyboard access and readable labels are demonstrated.
lessons.interview: Why flush asynchronous updates?
lessons.visual: An appointment selector with a visible keyboard focus path through four UI states

lessons.title: Shadow DOM and component boundaries
lessons.outcome: Keep DOM, styling, and event contracts inside their intended boundaries and understand the implications for optional legacy migration.
lessons.task: Show owned queries, scoped styles, and a stable public event contract.
lessons.acceptance: No private child DOM is accessed by the parent. The event detail carries the required business identity. Optional Aura work is labeled separately.
lessons.interview: Why can a global selector fail?
lessons.visual: Two component boxes with protected interiors connected by one public event port

lessons.title: Platform Events and publication timing
lessons.outcome: Publish a business fact with a deliberate relationship to commit, and verify the subscriber independently from the publisher.
lessons.task: Create a minimal event path with explicit commit behavior and a duplicate-safe receipt.
lessons.acceptance: Payload contains no unnecessary customer data. Publication timing is stated and checked. The receipt remains unique across repeated delivery.
lessons.interview: Why prefer After Commit for this fact?
lessons.visual: A committed appointment followed by separate publication delivery and receipt milestones

lessons.title: Change Data Capture, replay, and duplicate delivery
lessons.outcome: Choose a record-change stream or business event and recover from disconnection without treating replay IDs as permanent business identities.
lessons.task: Analyze the supplied trace and design both short-disconnection and retention-gap recovery.
lessons.acceptance: The duplicate produces one effect. Replay tokens are treated as opaque. Beyond-retention recovery is defined.
lessons.interview: What does CDC communicate?
lessons.visual: An interrupted event stream reconnecting with one repeated message safely ignored

lessons.title: Git fetch, integration, and cherry-picking a fix
lessons.outcome: Explain the state changed by common Git operations and transfer one focused correction without losing unrelated work.
lessons.task: Create the controlled branch experiment and explain each state transition.
lessons.acceptance: Working tree, index, branch, and remote-tracking state are distinguished. The selected commit is identified from real history. The final content is coherent and unrelated changes are preserved.
lessons.interview: Does fetch update your current files?
lessons.visual: A focused commit moving between two small branch histories

lessons.title: Pull requests, CI checks, and controlled deployment
lessons.outcome: Prepare a reviewable change with truthful validation, metadata dependencies, explicit target environment, and recovery steps.
lessons.task: Create a focused PR and release checklist for one completed Middle feature.
lessons.acceptance: No check is marked passed without evidence. Target org and permissions are explicit. Recovery includes data and external effects where relevant.
lessons.interview: What does a local Jest pass prove?
lessons.visual: A focused change passing through review validation deployment and user verification gates

lessons.title: Verifying an application under failure
lessons.outcome: Test the complete path from user action through background work and mocked provider response to the final visible result.
lessons.task: Verify the integrated feature with controlled failures and one repaired defect.
lessons.acceptance: Duplicate and denied-access cases are included. UI messages match persisted outcomes. No unexecuted check is reported as successful.
lessons.interview: Why can isolated tests all pass while the feature fails?
lessons.visual: A complete request path tested by several controlled failure switches

lessons.title: Enhanced Omni-Channel routing
lessons.outcome: Explain how queued service work becomes eligible for a person based on presence, capacity, and routing configuration, with a complete no-license simulation path.
lessons.task: Submit the provided simulation with three condition changes and an optional separately labeled live observation.
lessons.acceptance: Every chosen or excluded person has a reason. No unsupported tie-breaking rule is invented. Simulation and live evidence are clearly separated.
lessons.interview: Why is a queue not enough?
lessons.visual: One queued case passing presence capacity and skill gates toward a single eligible worker

lessons.title: Agentforce tasks, actions, and evidence
lessons.outcome: Build a clear mental model of an employee agent and verify one bounded read-only action before considering actions that change CRM data.
lessons.task: Complete the ten-case matrix for the read-only contract and optionally demonstrate the live action.
lessons.acceptance: No artificial slot is described as real calendar availability. Unknown and denied inputs are handled explicitly. Simulation and live results are distinguished.
lessons.interview: What does an action add beyond instructions?
lessons.visual: A conversational request connected to one read-only action and a verified result card

lessons.title: Automotive Cloud data modeling
lessons.outcome: Compare the small custom vehicle model with Automotive Cloud's industry entities and decide what additional business requirements would justify the product.
lessons.task: Map the Northstar customer-and-vehicle lifecycle and defend whether additional industry capabilities are needed.
lessons.acceptance: Vehicle__c is not confused with the industry Vehicle API. Relationships are not invented from labels. No unavailable trial blocks the core course.
lessons.interview: Why separate a Vehicle Definition?
lessons.visual: One vehicle model definition linked to individual cars and their changing participant relationships

lessons.title: Middle project review and technical defense
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate a coherent Northstar feature, defend its design with evidence, and repair one unfamiliar failure without relying on optional product licenses.
lessons.task: Deliver the integrated project and complete a short review plus one repair exercise.
lessons.acceptance: Access, duplicate handling, failure recovery, and bulk behavior are supported by evidence. The release plan declares dependencies and actual checks. Required clinic analyses are complete without mandatory live product licenses.
lessons.interview: Which risks should be handed to the next developer?
lessons.visual: A completed service feature surrounded by clear evidence cards and one repaired fault

courses.title: Senior Salesforce Developer
courses.entry: You can deliver a Middle-level feature with Apex, LWC, tests, and integrations, and are ready to investigate uncertain requirements and existing-system behavior.
courses.exit: Explain and verify a bounded improvement with evidence, access and reliability reasoning, a reviewable change, and a realistic recovery plan. Completion does not guarantee a professional job title.
courses.project: Northstar Motors grows into a dealer network. Improve its custom Vehicle__c and Test_Drive__c learning application while preserving correct access, booking outcomes, and recoverable integrations.

modules.title: Understand execution and measure the problem

lessons.title: How a Salesforce Transaction Runs
lessons.outcome: Distinguish application metadata, business records, and execution state.
lessons.task: Create a one-page diagram and a state table for Anna's booking. Use the synthetic trace; no Salesforce connection is required.
lessons.acceptance: The diagram has explicit commit boundaries and does not claim Hyperforce removes limits. A worker failure leaves the committed appointment intact. Every claim is labelled as a documented platform rule, a synthetic case result, or an observation from your own experiment.
lessons.interview: Which transaction boundary determines whether a failed follow-up can undo a saved booking?
lessons.visual: A booking transaction ends at a commit gate; a later notification has its own boundary.

lessons.title: Turn a Performance Complaint into a Measurable Requirement
lessons.outcome: Define latency, throughput, and backlog in plain terms.
lessons.task: Choose two journeys from the synthetic intake sheet and prepare a one-page investigation brief for Oleg.
lessons.acceptance: Latency, throughput, and backlog are not treated as interchangeable. Synthetic estimates and actual observations are visibly separated. The brief states sample limitations and a next evidence-gathering step.
lessons.interview: How would you investigate two users who disagree about whether Salesforce is slow?
lessons.visual: Different complaints become separate latency, throughput, and backlog measurements.

lessons.title: Locate Delay Across the Browser, Apex, and Database
lessons.outcome: Distinguish elapsed request time from Apex CPU time.
lessons.task: Explain the synthetic timeline, then design a small experiment that could confirm or reject one bottleneck hypothesis.
lessons.acceptance: The answer does not equate CPU, network elapsed time, and database duration. The proposed experiment changes one relevant factor and preserves the business result. Any measured result includes conditions and sample count; supplied timings remain marked synthetic.
lessons.interview: Why can a request take several seconds while Apex CPU remains low?
lessons.visual: A browser request contains server work; elapsed time and Apex CPU are different measurements.

lessons.title: Estimate Resource Demand Before Increasing Traffic
lessons.outcome: Separate per-transaction constraints from shared allocations.
lessons.task: Model all three traffic scenarios using the supplied assumptions and a small optional collection experiment.
lessons.acceptance: Every calculated value includes its unit and assumptions. The 80-versus-100 example produces 600 additional waiting items after 30 minutes. No small-org result is described as a validated 1000-bookings-per-minute capacity.
lessons.interview: How would you identify the first capacity constraint before increasing traffic?
lessons.visual: Transaction budgets and shared workload demand are shown as distinct constraints.

lessons.title: Choose an Optimization and Prove Its Value
lessons.outcome: Rank candidate changes without promising unsupported speedups.
lessons.task: Choose two candidates from the evidence cards and prepare an approval-ready optimization note.
lessons.acceptance: The recommendation follows evidence and business use rather than the amount of code changed. No exact speedup is promised without observed comparable measurements. The verification plan includes permissions and data correctness, not only response time.
lessons.interview: When is leaving imperfect code unchanged the better engineering choice?
lessons.visual: Two evidence-backed improvements are selected from five competing proposals.

lessons.title: Read Query Plans and Data Selectivity
lessons.outcome: Define selectivity and explain why an index is not a performance guarantee.
lessons.task: Compare the two synthetic snapshots and design a correct upcoming-appointments query for Anna.
lessons.acceptance: The answer explains why unchanged code can behave differently after data growth. The narrower query retains all records required by the stated user journey. Small-org observations and large-volume assumptions are reported separately.
lessons.interview: Why can a query slow down when its text has not changed?
lessons.visual: A broad status filter and a narrow business filter select different portions of the same data.

lessons.title: Find Shared Records Behind Lock Contention
lessons.outcome: Explain record locking, contention, and different forms of data skew.
lessons.task: Create a lock map and a processing plan for the synthetic three-worker case.
lessons.acceptance: The explanation identifies the common resource rather than only repeating UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW. The proposed partition corresponds to the actual record being contested. The recovery plan preserves failed work and does not rely on unlimited immediate retries.
lessons.interview: Why might updates to different appointment records compete for the same lock?
lessons.visual: Concurrent child updates compete for one hot vehicle record.

lessons.title: Load Data with Reconciliation and Safe Replays
lessons.outcome: Define a stable import identity separate from file row position.
lessons.task: Prepare a preflight and result ledger for the six supplied appointment rows, plus a separate vehicle fixture V-001 through V-005.
lessons.acceptance: The ledger never relies on CSV position as the permanent identity. A-101 version 1 is recorded as superseded before upload; the five-row submitted set has one snapshot per source identity. Successful, failed, and unprocessed outcomes are distinguishable; replay does not create extra appointments.
lessons.interview: How would you recover an import with successful, failed, and unprocessed rows?
lessons.visual: A dependent data load separates successful, failed, and unprocessed records.

lessons.title: Archive History Without Losing the Business Record
lessons.outcome: Distinguish archiving, deletion, backup, and audit history.
lessons.task: Use ten fictional appointments to define an archive policy proposal, a manifest, and a retrieval test.
lessons.acceptance: Archiving, backup, history, and deletion are not conflated. The exercise does not present an invented retention period as a legal rule. The design includes destination permissions and recovery, not only reduced live record count.
lessons.interview: What must be proven before old records can leave the operational system?
lessons.visual: Archived appointments remain discoverable through an explicit manifest and controlled retrieval path.

lessons.title: Design Record Access for a Dealer Network
lessons.outcome: Separate job capabilities from record visibility.
lessons.task: Compare individual appointment ownership with a centralized ownership alternative using the same business matrix.
lessons.acceptance: Peer access is not assumed from job title or role name. Removing one grant is not automatically treated as removal of every access path. The decision includes staff movement and exception cleanup as well as today's visibility.
lessons.interview: How does a salesperson moving between dealers challenge your sharing model?
lessons.visual: Dealer isolation and selected shared service access form a deliberate record-access model.

lessons.title: Remove Excess Access Without Breaking Legitimate Work
lessons.outcome: Trace additive permissions and independent record-access paths.
lessons.task: Use the inventory to remove the expired East collaboration while preserving legitimate West work.
lessons.acceptance: Muting is never described as a user-wide deny. The plan checks independent grants after each removal. Legitimate West work remains a specific acceptance criterion.
lessons.interview: Why can access remain after you remove a permission or sharing rule?
lessons.visual: Muting one permission group leaves an independent direct grant active.

lessons.title: Plan a Deferred-Sharing Maintenance Window
lessons.outcome: Explain what sharing-rule deferral does and does not pause.
lessons.task: Prepare a runbook and three failure-card responses for a synthetic Northstar access change.
lessons.acceptance: Resume and full Recalculate are explicit separate requirements. The plan acknowledges mechanisms that are not paused by sharing-rule deferral. Completion requires verified access and resolved exceptions, not only saved configuration.
lessons.interview: What remains unfinished if the operator stops after Resume?
lessons.visual: The procedure separates resuming calculations from recalculating accumulated changes and verifying access.

lessons.title: Control Privileged Code and External-User Access
lessons.outcome: Explain why authentication is not authorization.
lessons.task: Design the authorization contract for a portal caller who may read only their own appointments.
lessons.acceptance: The contract does not trust a client-supplied customer Id as proof of ownership. Identity, CRUD/FLS, record sharing, and payload validation are treated separately. Any elevated operation has a narrow purpose and explicit negative tests.
lessons.interview: When is privileged Apex justified, and how would you limit its authority?
lessons.visual: An external caller reaches a specific allowed action through separate identity, access, and input checks.

lessons.title: Choose System Boundaries and Data Ownership
lessons.outcome: Distinguish a system of record from a copied view.
lessons.task: Complete the ownership worksheet and choose an interaction pattern for each fact.
lessons.acceptance: A copy is never mistaken for the authoritative decision. The user-facing status matches the actual confirmation guarantee. Each asynchronous or replicated flow has a way to find and resolve missing work.
lessons.interview: Which facts should Salesforce own, copy, or read from another system?
lessons.visual: Salesforce, stock, and scheduling systems own different business facts.

lessons.title: Handle Duplicate and Out-of-Order Events
lessons.outcome: Separate event identity, operation identity, and stream position.
lessons.task: Apply the synthetic events to an appointment state and record a decision for every arrival.
lessons.acceptance: The older version cannot revert the newer state. The duplicate cancellation does not repeat the business effect. The answer explains why the same policy would not automatically work for delta events. External status labels stay separate from the starter picklist until a documented mapping or metadata extension exists.
lessons.interview: How can a repeatable business effect be safe when delivery can repeat?
lessons.visual: Duplicates and stale events are recorded without reversing the accepted appointment state.

lessons.title: Recover from an External-Service Outage Without a Retry Storm
lessons.outcome: Classify failures before retrying them.
lessons.task: Design the statuses and transitions for scheduling requests during a synthetic thirty-minute outage.
lessons.acceptance: No path retries forever without a bound or operator state. Unknown outcomes preserve the same business operation identity. The recovery calculation separates new arrivals from backlog drain and is labelled hypothetical.
lessons.interview: How would you restore a backlog without overwhelming a recovered dependency?
lessons.visual: Retries are delayed and limited, while recovery releases queued work gradually.

lessons.title: Reconstruct an Incident from Business and Technical Evidence
lessons.outcome: Distinguish symptom, contributing condition, and demonstrated cause.
lessons.task: Explain the synthetic N-77 notification incident and propose a safe recovery and prevention plan.
lessons.acceptance: The report distinguishes queuing success from downstream completion. The timeout remains an uncertain remote outcome until reconciled. Corrective actions can be verified and avoid blame-only explanations.
lessons.interview: How would you distinguish a missing notification from a misleading success log?
lessons.visual: The timeline distinguishes known events from an unresolved provider outcome.

modules.title: Change and release an existing system

lessons.title: Refactor Legacy Automation in Small Verified Steps
lessons.outcome: Explain characterization tests and their limits.
lessons.task: Design a small refactor that separates status-transition decisions from reminder persistence.
lessons.acceptance: Existing behavior and intended corrected behavior are labelled separately. The first change has one responsibility and a clear comparison path. Tests check side-effect counts and bulk behavior, not only line coverage.
lessons.interview: How would you safely change a trigger whose behavior is poorly understood?
lessons.visual: A single responsibility is separated from legacy automation while surrounding behavior remains under test.

lessons.title: Test Integration Contracts at the Right Boundaries
lessons.outcome: Explain consumer and provider contracts in plain language.
lessons.task: Prepare fixtures and tests for a provider moving from the old flat response to the proposed nested contract.
lessons.acceptance: An unfamiliar status cannot become Confirmed by default. The report identifies mocked dependencies and contract versions. At least one test would fail if the required reservation reference disappeared.
lessons.interview: Which test catches the highest-risk contract change at the lowest useful boundary?
lessons.visual: Different tests check local mapping, provider compatibility, and the user-facing result.

lessons.title: Release Metadata and Data Changes in Separate Stages
lessons.outcome: Separate deploying capability from moving data and switching users.
lessons.task: Write a staged release plan for adding the provider reference to existing and new appointments.
lessons.acceptance: Old supported clients remain compatible during the agreed transition. The backfill does not overwrite a newer authoritative value blindly. Code rollback and data recovery have separate inputs, owners, and checks.
lessons.interview: Why is a code rollback not a complete data recovery plan?
lessons.visual: Metadata expansion, data migration, and retirement of the old contract are separate stages.

lessons.title: Write an Architecture Decision and Review the Risk
lessons.outcome: Write a concise architecture decision record with real alternatives.
lessons.task: Write the booking-confirmation ADR and evaluate a helper that accepts any appointment Id before a privileged cancellation.
lessons.acceptance: Alternatives are compared under the same business requirements. The review distinguishes harmful behavior from stylistic preference. The explanation connects access mode, caller authority, and a negative test.
lessons.interview: How would you defend a decision while fairly representing its strongest alternative?
lessons.visual: An architecture choice and a code review are connected to concrete business and security consequences.

modules.title: Evaluate products and defend the final design

lessons.title: Evaluate Agentforce Actions, Access, and Failure Behavior
lessons.outcome: Separate conversational quality from action correctness.
lessons.task: Turn the eight synthetic cases into a reviewable test suite with action, access, and outcome criteria.
lessons.acceptance: The suite checks actual action outcomes and access boundaries, not only response quality. A repeated request cannot silently create a second booking. Transcript analysis is not represented as a completed live-agent test.
lessons.interview: What evidence would make an Agentforce write action ready for release?
lessons.visual: Agent evaluation covers allowed actions, unknown facts, denied records, retries, and confirmation.

lessons.title: Compare Core Salesforce, Automotive Cloud, and a DMS
lessons.outcome: Create a fit-gap comparison with explicit assumptions.
lessons.task: Compare the three options for the five synthetic requirements and identify the next decision-changing proof.
lessons.acceptance: Vehicle__c is not described as the installed Automotive Cloud Vehicle model. All options receive a fair comparison with operating consequences. Unverified capabilities and commercial assumptions are clearly labelled.
lessons.interview: When is extending an industry product better than maintaining a custom core model?
lessons.visual: Build, extend, and integrate options are compared against the same dealership requirements.

lessons.title: Lead a 45-Minute Dealer-Network Architecture Interview
lessons.outcome: Ask questions that change the design before drawing components.
lessons.task: Record or write a forty-five-minute architecture discussion using the synthetic requirement card.
lessons.acceptance: The design explains one complete user journey and at least one failure. Tradeoffs change when the business requirement changes. No unmeasured rate, product entitlement, or hidden platform implementation is presented as fact.
lessons.interview: Which part of your dealer-network design would fail first, and how would you detect it?
lessons.visual: The candidate revises a coherent booking design when an important requirement changes.

lessons.title: Capstone: Improve Northstar with Reproducible Evidence
lessons.outcome: Produce evidence that matches the scope of an improvement claim.
lessons.task: Implement and verify two bounded, connected improvements using either a small Salesforce environment or the explicit local-proxy path.
lessons.acceptance: At least one implementation path was executed; otherwise the submission explicitly remains incomplete for implementation acceptance. Before-and-after claims are supported by comparable observations and unchanged business assertions. The package includes tests, limitations, recovery reasoning, and no real customer data or credentials.
lessons.interview: What can another reviewer reproduce from your capstone evidence, and what remains unproven?
lessons.visual: The capstone connects a concrete improvement to reproducible evidence and an explicit recovery plan.

courses.title: Salesforce Job Research
courses.entry: A target role or an interest in finding your next Salesforce position.
courses.exit: A repeatable search workflow, an honest CV, a reviewable portfolio and an interview practice plan.
courses.project: Your own job-search workspace and evidence-based application materials.

lessons.title: Choose a Target Role and Read Job Requirements
lessons.outcome: Turn a vague goal into a shortlist of roles and a skills map you can support with examples.
lessons.task: Choose a realistic target using five current job descriptions.
lessons.acceptance: No requirement is marked essential unless the description supports that interpretation. Tutorial work is identified as practice rather than employment. The chosen target is explained with evidence, not only a desired title.
lessons.interview: Does a senior title prove that two roles require the same skills?
lessons.visual: a simple map with three career paths and one clearly selected route

lessons.title: Use AI to Research and Verify Job Opportunities
lessons.outcome: Use an AI assistant to organise job research while checking every opportunity against a real employer source.
lessons.task: Research a small batch of roles and verify the strongest candidates.
lessons.acceptance: No role is accepted solely on an AI-generated link or summary. Unknown conditions remain explicitly unknown. The list includes a date checked and a direct source for each active opportunity.
lessons.interview: What if the assistant cannot browse?
lessons.visual: a magnifying glass checking one job card while duplicate cards sit aside

lessons.title: Build a Repeatable Job Search Workflow
lessons.outcome: Create a small system that makes the next useful action visible without turning job hunting into administration.
lessons.task: Build and run a small job-search board for one week.
lessons.acceptance: Applied means actually submitted. Unverified opportunities cannot silently enter the application queue. Every active record has a next step; closed records retain their useful history.
lessons.interview: Why not create dozens of stages?
lessons.visual: a calm task board with one job card moving toward a calendar tile

lessons.title: Describe Your Experience with Evidence
lessons.outcome: Explain what you built, why it mattered and what you can actually prove.
lessons.task: Write two evidence-based accounts: one completed feature and one problem you investigated.
lessons.acceptance: The reader can distinguish your work from the team’s or starter project’s work. Every number has a measurement source and scope. Training work is labelled and still explains a meaningful technical result.
lessons.interview: Must every CV achievement include a percentage?
lessons.visual: a developer connecting a project card to a test result and a small evidence folder

lessons.title: Write a Clear and Honest Salesforce CV
lessons.outcome: Create a readable CV that connects your skills to relevant work without inventing experience.
lessons.task: Produce a master CV based only on experience and projects you can substantiate.
lessons.acceptance: The target role and two relevant examples are easy to find. No training project is presented as commercial employment. The exported file has readable text, working links and current contact details.
lessons.interview: Should you claim expertise in a tool you used once?
lessons.visual: a clean document beside a pencil and a small verified project card

lessons.title: Tailor Your CV to a Specific Role
lessons.outcome: Change emphasis for a vacancy while keeping your experience accurate and consistent.
lessons.task: Tailor your master CV to one verified vacancy and keep a change log.
lessons.acceptance: Every claim remains consistent with the master CV. The most relevant evidence is prominent. Unsupported requirements are recorded as gaps rather than disguised as experience.
lessons.interview: What should change when tailoring a CV?
lessons.visual: two simple documents linked by three carefully selected matching cards

lessons.title: Prepare a Salesforce Portfolio for Review
lessons.outcome: Make one project easy for another developer to understand, run and assess.
lessons.task: Prepare one portfolio repository and rehearse a short review walkthrough.
lessons.acceptance: Training context, ownership and limitations are explicit. Setup and test instructions match the project. The demonstration includes a success and a failure case.
lessons.interview: Does a screenshot prove reproducibility?
lessons.visual: an open project folder with a small application preview and a clear checklist

lessons.title: Practise a Technical Interview with AI
lessons.outcome: Run a structured mock interview that reveals gaps instead of rewarding memorised wording.
lessons.task: Run a five-question mock interview and turn it into a small practice plan.
lessons.acceptance: The session contains follow-up questions, not only definitions. Corrections are supported or explicitly marked uncertain. The final plan names a concrete exercise rather than “study more.”
lessons.interview: Is an AI interview score a reliable hiring prediction?
lessons.visual: two drawn people discussing a technical card with a small evidence checklist

lessons.title: Practise Live Coding and Code Review
lessons.outcome: Show your reasoning while solving a small problem and reviewing a flawed implementation.
lessons.task: Implement the input-only count method, then review a deliberately flawed alternative.
lessons.acceptance: Counts use only the supplied list. Empty input and repeated vehicles are covered. The review identifies behaviour and scaling issues before style preferences. The report names the tested class, API version, actual test result and zero-query/zero-DML method check; unexecuted org checks are labelled outstanding.
lessons.interview: Why clarify whether database queries are allowed?
lessons.visual: a developer at a simple code window with a peer pointing to one review note

lessons.title: Discuss Your Experience and Evaluate the Employer
lessons.outcome: Prepare clear experience stories and questions that help you understand the work and team.
lessons.task: Prepare three experience stories and a focused set of employer questions.
lessons.acceptance: Stories contain a specific action and evidence, not only personal qualities. Team contributions and limitations remain accurate. Employer questions clarify responsibilities you care about.
lessons.interview: Should a mistake story hide the mistake?
lessons.visual: a balanced conversation between two drawn people with three simple question cards

lessons.title: Build a Preparation Plan from Interview Feedback
lessons.outcome: Turn an interview or mock session into a focused cycle of practice and reassessment.
lessons.task: Turn one interview or mock session into a one-week preparation plan.
lessons.acceptance: Each priority has a concrete practice task and a verification method. The plan fits the time you actually have. Reassessment uses a variation, not only the original question.
lessons.interview: Can you know why an employer rejected you without feedback?
lessons.visual: a small calendar beside a learning loop and two focused task cards
